after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
The first three terms of the binomial expansion for $(1+x)^{n}$ are given by

$$
{(1+x)}^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

By substituting $x=-\frac{b}{3}$ and $n=8$ into the above formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1-\frac{b}{3})}^{8} & =1+8\cdot (-\frac{b}{3})+\frac{8(8-1)}{2!}\cdot {(-\frac{b}{3})}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{8b}{3}+\frac{8\cdot 7}{2}\cdot \frac{{b}^{2}}{9}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{8b}{3}+28\cdot \frac{{b}^{2}}{9}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{8b}{3}+\frac{28{b}^{2}}{9}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Expanding a Binomial With Negative Coefficients
content.worked_solution:
The first three terms of the binomial expansion for $(1+x)^{n}$ are given by

$$
{(1+x)}^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

By substituting $x=-\frac{b}{3}$ and $n=8$ into the above formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1-\frac{b}{3})}^{8} & =1+8\cdot (-\frac{b}{3})+\frac{8(8-1)}{2!}\cdot {(-\frac{b}{3})}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{8b}{3}+\frac{8\cdot 7}{2}\cdot \frac{{b}^{2}}{9}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{8b}{3}+28\cdot \frac{{b}^{2}}{9}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{8b}{3}+\frac{28{b}^{2}}{9}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
The first three terms of the binomial expansion for $(1+x)^{n}$ are given by

$$
{(1+x)}^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

By substituting $x=-\frac{5c}{2}$ and $n=6$ into the above formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1-\frac{5c}{2})}^{6} & =1+6\cdot (-\frac{5c}{2})+\frac{6(6-1)}{2!}\cdot {(-\frac{5c}{2})}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-15c+\frac{6\cdot 5}{2}\cdot \frac{25{c}^{2}}{4}+⋯ \\  & =1-15c+15\cdot \frac{25{c}^{2}}{4}+⋯ \\  & =1-15c+\frac{375{c}^{2}}{4}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

In particular, the ${x}^{4}$ term is given by

$$
\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)}{4!}{x}^{4}.
$$

Replacing $x$ with $-3m$ and $n$ with $7$ in the above expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7(7-1)(7-2)(7-3)}{4!}\cdot (-3m)^{4} & =\frac{7\cdot 6\cdot 5\cdot 4}{24}\cdot (-3)^{4}\cdot {m}^{4} \\  & =35\cdot 81{m}^{4} \\  & =2835{m}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coefficient of ${m}^{4}$ is $2835.$
